title: typeof, instanceof, and safe type checks
hook: `typeof` is the fastest runtime type question in JavaScript — but it lies about `null` and arrays. Learn when to pair it with `instanceof`, `Array.isArray`, and strict equality instead.

blocks.text: JavaScript has no compile-time type checker — you discover types at **run time** with operators and helpers. **`typeof`** returns a string for primitives and a coarse label for objects (`'object'`, `'function'`). **`instanceof`** walks the prototype chain to test constructor ancestry. **`Array.isArray`** is the reliable array test. **`Object.prototype.toString.call(value)`** can distinguish built-in object brands when `typeof` and `instanceof` are not enough.

entries.plainDefinition: Unary operator returning a string: 'undefined', 'boolean', 'number', 'bigint', 'string', 'symbol', 'function', or 'object'.
Tests whether an object's prototype chain includes a constructor's `.prototype`. Works across realms only for built-ins in some cases.
The spec-correct way to detect arrays. Works for cross-realm arrays where `instanceof` can fail.
A legacy bug: `typeof null === 'object'`. Always test `value === null` separately.

blocks.text: API handlers receive untyped payloads. Before calling `.map()` you must know you have an array — `typeof x === 'object'` is true for arrays, `null`, dates, and plain objects alike. A guard like `if (data && typeof data === 'object' && Array.isArray(data.items))` prevents run-time crashes. In C#, the compiler catches type errors before deploy; in JavaScript you write defensive checks or use TypeScript to catch them at build time.

blocks.title: Compile-time vs run-time
blocks.body: TypeScript `typeof x` at compile time is a type query. JavaScript `typeof x` at run time returns a string. C# `typeof(T)` returns a `System.Type` object at compile time. Three different tools with the same keyword.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Null? → strict equality
items.body: `x === null` — never rely on `typeof` for null.

items.title: Array? → Array.isArray
items.body: Do not use `typeof`, `instanceof` alone in iframes, or `Array.isArray` alternatives in hot paths without reason.

items.title: Custom class? → instanceof
items.body: `error instanceof TypeError` — but remember prototype chain can be broken in tests.

items.title: Plain object? → Object.prototype.toString or duck typing

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using `typeof x === 'object'` without excluding `null`. Using `instanceof Array` in cross-realm code. Confusing TypeScript compile-time `typeof` with JavaScript run-time `typeof`. Using `constructor` property for type checks — it can be spoofed.

blocks.text: The `typeof null === 'object'` bug is a TC39-documented legacy behavior: in the original implementation, values were 32-bit tags plus payload; null was all-zero bits, same tag as objects. Changing it would break millions of sites. Production pattern: `value != null` (checks both null and undefined) or explicit `value === null` before object operations. For `undefined`, `typeof` is reliable. `instanceof` uses `GetPrototypeOf` internally — polyfilled environments or broken `@@hasInstance` can fool it. `Symbol.toStringTag` on built-ins makes `Object.prototype.toString.call(new Map())` return `'[object Map]'`.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing why `typeof null` is `'object'`. Using only `typeof x === 'object'` for object guards. Claiming TypeScript types exist at run time. Not mentioning `Array.isArray` for arrays.

interviewTakeaways: `typeof null === 'object'` is a historical bug — always use `x === null`.
Use `Array.isArray()` for arrays, not `typeof` or `instanceof` alone.
TypeScript `typeof` is compile-time; JavaScript `typeof` is run-time string.
`instanceof` walks the prototype chain; can fail cross-realm for built-ins.
60s: typeof for primitives. null needs ===. Array.isArray for arrays. typeof null is object bug from engine tags.
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'typeof null is object so null is an object.' Strong: 'Legacy bug — null is primitive, check with === null.'
Guarding objects with only `typeof x === 'object'` — null slips through.
Strong answer: 'typeof for primitives, === null for null, Array.isArray for arrays, instanceof for custom classes.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS `typeof foo` at compile time infers types from values. At run time you still need JS `typeof` for string labels.
C# `is`/`as` are compile-time aware and return typed bindings. JS has no `as` — you guard manually or use TS assertions (no run-time effect).
